## Design

### 2026-10-05 – October 5th: Learning Onshape and CAD modelling

**4h**

October 5th: Learning Onshape and CAD modelling

This session was entirely focused on learning how CADs worked. I've never really used them so I wanted to get a bit of experience. I tried a lot of different CADs such as Shapr3D, Tinkercad, and Autodesk Fusion, which took up a lot of time, but what worked best was Onshape. I found it out through people guiding me through the Hack Club Slack forum, so thanks to that.
I did the Bakebuild Onshape tutorial provided by Hack Club. These are some of the Cookie cutters I made:
![D cookie](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/0f4385d85e4458ae4a4aa64bd5276d04c3431eadca538d64dcc0466334557c89.png)
![Untitled](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/312b0fbaf662e5224079cf6cb96ee0ac1a542be5d4d33a4a94f295dbec515c56.png)
They aren't the best, but they did help me understand how it worked. Then I spent some time playing around with Onshape, and after about an hour or so, I was able to make a sofa. I think it really helped me grasp the fundamentals and understand how the CAD worked.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/374327148ad440076971cec98accd3952f5c2543cf71c7cdf57f49daf9d42cae.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/cefc87015152b34ff89513136f53ce3ac6a9783cc32c419fa586b3edb8caca21.png)
I also watched a few tutorials, and I found this one very useful:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/addd7cfc531e890e4dee04489e2fd6841312123840f990ee87ebf75add681d07.png)

### 2026-10-05 – October 6th: Beginning the project, Making the PCB, Schematic, and BOM.

**7h**

October 6th: Beginning the project, Making the PCB, Schematic, and BOM.

So first, I started to brainstorm ideas because I didn't want it to be a boring copy of the starbie project, so I decided to make it more of like a handheld console kinda thing with 3 buttons, removing the sensors. This was my original rough plan of what it would look like.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/f17a6059581ecfa8e0170658adbe400f3c7f856f57ae167456bb5b77862601bb.png)
So I started building it in Kicad. I also had to kind of learn how to use Kicad as it was my first time. I watched a few tutorials and using help from the starbie project guide I got to this:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/4f33b0d509b45ee78b74abdac5b9f0cf00f15c1ae65bc595bef0db7e39ee532c.png)
Then I made the PCB, which was a little annoying to learn cuz the interface  wasn't very intuitive and i had trouble with part footprint libraries and stuff. But eventually I got to this.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/dcf0f33189000916d40c8a5513c2bf70042fc329032c250d3cc4c4b5a317af43.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/d7198a2f16736aa013647e8a8de878acb810184e4fe9620108180fcf3ca3aee1.png)
Then I started to look for parts on Aliexpress, but then I realized how expensive the XIAO ESP32 C3 was, and it took up half of my budget. It was around $15-$17 dollars. With my other parts, it came to about $31 dollars before pcb manufacturing and 3d printing costs. This took up most of my time. After a really long time of searching, I still couldn't find anything, the closest being $27.50.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/b49cfa274f709b403516511c8c47627fb417f597ee74d8966ab9fb45e2c778b5.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/fe604d25ffed05da0656a0106392cb49486705d597763e3f91f3f37b08f07536.png)
So after an unsuccessful search for parts, I finally came to the conclusion that I wouldn't be able to use the XIAO ESP32 C3 and that I'm going to have to use something else like the base model ESP32 C3 SuperMini, which is far cheaper.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/a0fe17fe1dfff91545d880f296292e647f84770f204e68a78355e2d0ea089ac5.png)
I also got a quote for the cost to make the PCB which is $2, and shipping is $1.5.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/2e8aac96a923ccf986f95b4e2518f9562bfd75d1a663adf84d28daee7c9fbdf4.png)
I'm going to have to redo the schematics and PCB with a new microcontroller.

Edit: Never mind, I won't have to, I just realized this whooole thing is in USD and not NZD, giving me a total NZD budget of $53.50. That should just be enough for Everything. That brings the total parts cost to $20.36 USD, $16.86 for parts and $3.5 for the PCB with shipping Included. But I will have to buy a Soldering Iron and some solder.

### 2026-10-07 – October 7th: Modelling the case in Onshape.

**4h**

October 7th: Modelling the case in Onshape.

This was reaaally frustrating. Importing the pieces was pretty hard. I had to find 3d models for the buttons i was using. That took quite a while, but eventually I got to this:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/6ddf86158581c5f1ec6f4cb2c9e781380c7c9ccc4a9196a00a7077f9b1ae38b2.png)
After that I had to make the case. I tried a bunch of different designs. At first I tried to make screw holes, then i switched to pillars, then I had to reinforce the pillars to make sure they didn't break. Finally, this was the design i thought worked best:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/7001ad8707a46e6af9c2350bd566d0457193a5f0a08ad2af31db6b8a347d9764.png)
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/de67751d48d865f043fe9b6d65cc7ecf7c675aed0cb9292d10c1b39847393c84.png)
The USB port was also a bigger challenge than you would expect. I had to figure out how to hide the components, then I messed around with the hole tool which didn't work, and I had to use the extrude tool. Then I realized that I had to make a bigger hole since the USB port didn't come all the way out, so the hole has to be quite big and ugly:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/4e4783c1ce596805e08ffbed788dfcefb1e7ae947b6238de05e18ba4c8076314.png)
Now I have to make the top part of the case, which I have no clue how to do. There are a lot of different options, but all of them are pretty hard to do. Currently, my best contender is a sliding contraption with a screw, but that's pretty hard to do, so I'll have to leave that for another session. I made progress this session, just not as much as I expected to.

### 2026-10-07 – October 8th: Finished the Case, Updated the BOM

**2.5h**

October 8th: Finished the Case, Updated the BOM

I finally finished the case, making the front case plate, with an attachable mechanism. This took me quite a while to think of and design, but I ended up making it. I made the attachable thing and the hole for the screen and buttons. Its obviously not the best thing in the world, but I'm pretty happy with it. Oh and for the model below I couldn't find a model for the button caps so it look a little weird.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/02a134ade0e6d6855f52193e9ed4713ecda7118bf67cbde839686f848508e1f1.png)
I also updated the BOM. I removed the Soldering Iron after advice from other people, and after including my 3d printed parts, the total cost is now down to $20.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/4b7dbdd52c21c7a5fa34b32a2397cee72a2b69ff9588d2297c0c4025b5257423.png)
I also made some temporary firmware for my Squarbie Macropad thing. Its kind of its own mini computer for now, but later on I'm gonna design an app on my computer than can let me control the macropad, display timers on it, set reminders, and control what the buttons do. I think this project was pretty cool, and I'm excited to hold the final product in my hands in a couple of weeks.
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6NsErT1120V2FDTcxwPhvTmpArnC2ArA/361030ca0ec29e48563a58a810f409b3e7b2e37af9c1a36cf3ff5930032c6809.png)
Now all I really have to do is update my Github Repo, verify my ID (there were problems with that so I reached out to support), and then I'm done! I can't really make the app for it yet until i get the parts, so for now it will just be a mini computer thing. Short but productive session today!
